forecasts.title: Will Bitcoin be above $85,000 by Sep 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET?
forecasts.reason: hunt chose NO but its own numbers refuse it: side price 0.97, own edge +2.0pt vs fee 0.2pt — It is the only shortlist market whose answer is a hard, checkable quantitative fact — current BTC spot versus a barrier, with ~36 hours left — so live price and realized-vol data give a decisive edge over a price that is just sitting on the minimum-tick floor.
forecasts.dossier:
RESOLUTION MECHANICS: Per the Kalshi record, this is a touch/barrier market — YES if the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) is above $85,000 at any minute from Aug 24, 2026 through Sep 11, 2026 11:59 PM ET, with immediate early resolution on a cross. It is still trading, so no touch has occurred in the 18 days the window has been open.

SPOT AND PATH: CoinDesk shows BTC at ~$77,161, down 1.6% on the day, after hotter-than-expected PPI drove a risk-off session; Yahoo has it opening $78,292 and sliding to $77,942 intraday. Spot-ETF flows flipped to $167M of outflows after a three-week inflow run. The barrier requires +10.2% from here inside ~36 hours. Since the window opened Aug 24, the highest print has been ~$81,455 (Sep 4 high $81,167) — BTC has never come within 4.4% of $85k during the measurement period, and it is now moving away from it.

BASE RATE / VOL MATH: August 2026 was BTC's best month of the year (+25%), so vol is not dead, but the recent weekly range ($76,877–$81,455, ~6%) implies daily sigma of roughly 2%. Over 1.5 days sigma is ~2.6%, so $85,000 is a ~4-sigma barrier. Reflection-principle touch probability under a normal is <0.1%; even assuming crypto tails an order of magnitude fatter than lognormal, that lands near 0.5–1%. Historically, no CPI print has produced a same-day 10% BTC rally — post-CPI BTC moves cluster at 1–5%.

CROWD NARRATIVE: The 3c/4c quote is not a considered forecast; it is the minimum-tick floor where cheap-lottery buyers and residual open interest from when $85k looked reachable (early September, BTC ~$81k) still sit. 24h tape is $8 across 13 trades — no informed flow is repricing it. The other side is buying a Sep-11 CPI melt-up plus a squeeze through $85k.

DISCONFIRMING OBSERVABLE: A dovish CPI surprise Sep 11 that takes BRTI back above ~$82,000 intraday would put the barrier inside 2 sigma of the remaining window and make me wrong; short of that, NO.
sources: Kalshi API market record for KXBTCPRICE-85000-26SEP11 (rules_primary/secondary, BRTI settlement, bid 0.03/ask 0.04, OI 3,673)
BLS release calendar: CPI scheduled 2026-09-11; PPI released 2026-09-10

forecasts.title: When will Anthropic officially announce an IPO?
forecasts.reason: hunt chose NO but its own numbers refuse it: side price 0.96, own edge +1.0pt vs fee 0.3pt — Resolution is gated by a hard, checkable SEC procedural clock (public S-1 must be on file 15 days before any roadshow) plus a dated Reuters timeline, so primary sources settle it mechanically rather than requiring a forecast of human behavior or volatility.
forecasts.dossier:
BASE RATE: For a US IPO, the three resolution triggers here (S-1 declared effective, IPO priced, exchange ticker assigned) all cluster within days of pricing, at the END of the process. From public S-1 flip to pricing is essentially never under ~3 weeks for a mega-deal, because SEC policy requires the issuer to publicly file at least 15 days before any roadshow, and roadshows themselves run 7-10 business days.

RESEARCH: Anthropic submitted a CONFIDENTIAL draft S-1 on June 1, 2026 (its own newsroom; CNBC). Critically, that self-announced filing did NOT resolve this market YES — strong evidence Kalshi is applying its strict three-prong test, not the loose market title. EDGAR shows no public S-1 or S-1/A as of today (Sept 9); it was still absent as of Aug 26. Reuters (Sept 5, 2026) reports the public S-1 has slipped to LATE SEPTEMBER and the roadshow to MID-OCTOBER at the earliest, targeting a late-October listing 'just days before the November midterms.' Working forward from the 15-day rule: even if the S-1 went public today, the roadshow could not start before Sept 24, making a pre-Oct-1 pricing arithmetically impossible. No ticker has been confirmed.

CROWD NARRATIVE: Headlines scream '$965B–$2T AI IPO, fall 2026,' and the market's title ('officially announce an IPO') reads far looser than its rules. That gap — plus lottery-ticket appeal on a marquee name with 561k volume — is what holds the price at 4-5c rather than 1c.

WHO'S ON THE OTHER SIDE: YES buyers are betting either that the deal accelerates dramatically, or that Kalshi loosely reads a proposed Nasdaq symbol printed on a late-September public S-1 ('we have applied to list under the symbol...') as 'a securities exchange has assigned a ticker.' I price that as roughly 45% chance of a public S-1 landing before Sept 30 times ~8% chance of the loose reading, since the secondary rule's framing ('even if the company does not start trading until after Oct 1') clearly targets the pricing stage.

WHAT WOULD PROVE ME WRONG: A public S-1/A appearing on EDGAR in the next few days containing a reserved Nasdaq ticker, followed by Kalshi guidance treating symbol reservation as assignment — or any report that Anthropic has compressed to a pre-Oct-1 pricing. Absent that, this is mechanically NO.

forecasts.title: Will Apple Inc. release iPhone 18 Pro before Oct 1, 2026?
forecasts.reason: hunt chose YES but its own numbers refuse it: side price 0.95, own edge +4.0pt vs fee 0.3pt — The one market whose outcome is verifiable against a hard, already-scheduled corporate event date rather than a probabilistic forecast, and research resolves the one genuine uncertainty (Apple's split-launch rumor) decisively in favor of YES.
forecasts.dossier: BASE RATE: Apple has released new flagship iPhones in September every year since 2012 (except the pandemic-shifted iPhone 12 in Oct 2020), and once an event is officially announced with a date, the product ships within ~10 days essentially 100% of the time. The only real uncertainty this cycle was the widely-reported plan to SPLIT the iPhone 18 lineup across two seasons. Research resolves it in favor of YES: Bloomberg-sourced reporting (MacRumors, 9to5Mac, Forbes, AppleInsider) confirms the SPLIT delays only the standard iPhone 18, 18e, and iPhone Air 2 to spring 2027, while the higher-margin iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launch this fall to protect holiday-quarter ASPs. Apple officially announced its 'Surprise and shine' event for Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at Apple Park; multiple outlets report preorders begin Saturday Sept 12 and units go on sale Friday Sept 18 — all before the Oct 1 cutoff. The event is literally tomorrow (today is Sept 8, 2026). CROWD NARRATIVE: The market sits at 0.94, likely still discounting lingering 'iPhone 18 delayed to 2027' headlines that actually referred only to the non-Pro models — a classic misread that distorts the price downward. This is precisely the underconfidence/compression-toward-50 bias the policy exploits: a near-certain favorite priced too cheap. WHO IS ON THE OTHER SIDE: NO holders are betting on a last-minute event cancellation or a resolution-definition quibble (e.g., 'release' meaning something other than on-sale date). Given the event invitation is already public and press embargoes are set, that is a fraction-of-a-percent tail. WHAT WOULD PROVE ME WRONG: Apple abruptly cancels or postpones the Sept 9 keynote (force majeure), or the Pro models are unveiled but pushed to on-sale after Oct 1 — neither of which any current supply-chain or press reporting supports. Honest probability 0.99.

forecasts.title: Will Apple Inc. release iPhone 18 Pro before Sep 21, 2026?
forecasts.reason: This is a near-deterministic factual event with an already-confirmed Apple event date and on-sale date, where primary-source research resolves nearly all uncertainty—unlike the speculative IPO/M&A/AGI markets.
forecasts.dossier: BASE RATE: Apple has launched its flagship Pro iPhones in September every year for over a decade, with the announcement in the first/second week and on-sale roughly a week later. iPhone 17 (2025): event Sept 9, on sale Sept 19. That base rate alone puts a September 18-19 2026 release near-certain. RESEARCH: Apple has now OFFICIALLY confirmed a keynote titled 'Surprise and shine' for September 9, 2026 (10am PT). Multiple outlets (MacRumors, AppleInsider, Forbes/David Phelan) report pre-orders begin Saturday Sept 12 and the iPhone 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max go on sale Friday, September 18, 2026. Both the announcement (Sept 9) and the on-sale date (Sept 18) fall before the Sept 21 cutoff—so under any reasonable reading of 'release' the market resolves YES. Notably, Apple is splitting its lineup this year: only the Pro/Pro Max/foldable launch in fall, while the base iPhone 18 and 18e slip to spring 2027—but that does NOT affect the Pro, which is the subject of this ticker. CROWD NARRATIVE: The price sits at 0.91, compressed toward 50c. The residual discount likely reflects generic 'delay risk' and thin volume (9 trades). But with the keynote date confirmed by Apple itself and the on-sale date a full three days inside the window, that discount is too large. WHO'S ON THE OTHER SIDE: NO holders are betting on a last-minute delay, a slip of the foldable dragging the whole event, or a technicality in 'release' meaning general availability landing after Sept 21. WHAT WOULD PROVE ME WRONG: Apple postponing the Sept 9 event, or pushing Pro availability past Sept 21 (e.g., a supply-chain or 2nm chip yield disaster). No such signal exists; reporting consistently points to Sept 18 sale. Honest probability ~0.97, small residual for genuine tail-risk of postponement within a 13-day window.
